title: Trading Platform (FREE early access) for Pro | Technical | Algo traders
author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
selftext:
[https://while25.com](https://while25.com)

I’m pretty sure most traders are using several disconnected tools in their workflow.

Your market data and charts are in one place, analysis somewhere else, and execution on another platform. You can build pipelines between them, but they still have gaps. For example, a TradingView webhook can send a signal, but it doesn’t really know what is happening with your orders, positions or order book.

After talking to a bunch of traders, we kept hearing 

three problems:  
1) Access to raw data  
2) Different platforms for different asset classes  
3) Too much friction between an idea and actually executing it

So we started building While25 from the ground up around one idea: **data, analysis, strategy development and execution should live in the same system.**

That turned out to be much harder than we expected. Handling financial data, different broker connections, real-time systems and a workspace where you can analyze, build and trade without breaking execution is a pretty deep engineering problem.

We eventually realized this is less of a “trading app” problem and more of a **data pipeline + real-time systems problem**.

So we decided to build it anyway. We’re almost ready to release the first build!

**What we have so far**  
1) Native order and risk management  
2) Built-in chart engine with TV-grade charts  
3) Direct broker data, so your charts and execution use the same feed  
4) Code editor with a Python SDK  
5) An AI assistant that can analyze your workspace and help build strategies, indicators and dashboards

The idea is to go from: **“I have an idea” → analyze → build → test → execute** without jumping between four different tools.

We don’t know yet how many people actually want this. But we’ve spent a lot of time building the underlying infrastructure and we’re excited to finally put it in people’s hands.

[https://while25.com](https://while25.com/)

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Having charts and execution on the same direct broker feed fixes a real gap in webhook setups, so that's a good design choice. I'd make sure the platform logs every signal, order and fill with timestamps, so users can measure slippage and compare backtest to live. An event calendar with accurate release times would also help, since Cymetica's EventTrader is one source of the earnings and macro timing that pro traders rely on around news. Good luck with the release.
